memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Ephron the Hittite was sitting among his people and he replied to Abraham in the hearing of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city. "No, my lord," he said. "Listen to me; I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. I give it to you in the presence of my people. Bury your dead." - Gen 23:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Ephron makes what sounds like a generous offer: "I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it." On the surface, it seems like a gift. But this was the customary way of bargaining in that culture - a public show of generosity that actually expected full payment, and often more. Abraham, wise to the ways of the world, understood this and would insist on paying the true price, as we'll see.

There is a practical wisdom here worth noticing. Abraham was gracious and humble, but he was not naive. He could receive kindness, but he could also discern when a situation called for careful, honest dealing rather than simply accepting things at face value. Godly people are called to be both gentle and wise.

Jesus taught exactly this balance: "Be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves" (Matt 10:16). We are to be pure and gracious, yes - but also discerning, not gullible. Faith does not mean checking our good sense at the door. It means combining a soft heart with a clear head.

This is a helpful reminder for how we move through the world. We honour God by being kind and trusting, but also by being wise and careful in our dealings, so that we act with true integrity and are not taken advantage of, nor take advantage of others. Ask God for both a gracious spirit and a discerning mind, that you may deal honestly and wisely in all things.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you combine a gracious heart with wise discernment?
- Where do you need to be both gentle and shrewd in your dealings?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me both a soft heart and a clear head. Help me be gracious and trusting, yet also wise and discerning, so that I deal honestly and rightly in all my affairs. Make me gentle and shrewd, like Jesus taught.
Amen.
